g_policy.reason: The offer copy states the 60-minute priority-routing reward before the user chooses to play. The decline and ad-failure paths leave normal access intact.

g_no_cash.reason: The reward is in-app priority routing, not cash or a transferable equivalent.

g_no_chat_content.reason: The trigger event restricts the card to users whose chats are mostly long roleplay stories. Determining whether chats are roleplay stories requires their content or topics.

g_no_free_removal.reason: The proposal says it removes nothing free, and its decline path keeps replies at their normal speed.

g_brand_safety.reason: The placement is a card in the s09 profile-menu drawer, a content-safe sheet away from chats.

c1_revealed_value.reason: The reward samples priority routing, which s02.e06 lists as a Janitor+ benefit.

c2_evidence.reason: The claim in “what makes it work here” about skipping a normal queue goes beyond s02.e06’s observed priority-routing benefit; m03 marks normal-priority routing as inferred. The model also does not establish the proposed targeting distinction of chats that are mostly long roleplay stories.

c4_protects_subscription.reason: The reward limits priority routing to 60 minutes, with a frequency cap of two plays per day.

c5_moment.reason: The card appears in the profile menu after the user returns from the Upgrade entry, rather than interrupting an active chat task.

c6_fits_simula.reason: The unit is a sponsored game triggered by an app-detectable return to the menu. The ad-failure path says unverified play does not turn on faster replies.

c7_specific.reason: The idea names the s09 Upgrade to Janitor Plus entry and samples the priority-routing benefit shown at s02.e06.
